title: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX module (bought), on a generated carrier

compute.frame: millimetres, the module's own datum: origin at the Ø1.80 locating hole at the lower left, SO-DIMM edge along the bottom (edge at y = -6.00, top edge at y = 39.00), x right, y up, seen from the top (as Figure 5-1 of the data sheet). The carrier around it is generated (src/system), so its outline, ports and header are ours, not NVIDIA's

source.where: DS-10712-001 v1.7, section 5.5 Module Drawing and Dimensions: 'Module Size: 69.6 mm x 45 mm'
section 5.5, Figure 5-1 Top View (page 48): 4X Ø3.20 at x 11.20 / 54.40 and y 4.41 / 33.21 from the datum hole

holes.note: read from the drawing's leader lines (symmetric about the GPU centroid at x 32.80, y 18.81); the module also has 2X Ø2.75 and Ø1.80 locating holes. Confirm against NVIDIA's module model before the carrier goes to fab

tallestMm.note: depends on the generated carrier's SO-DIMM connector and the chosen heatsink or fan, neither of which is the module's: the module itself is 4.08 mm max above and 5.08 mm max below its 1.20 mm PCB (Figure 5-1 side view)

at.note: the module has no header: the generated carrier places one and level-shifts it

pins.note: set by the generated carrier; the module signals it can route are under moduleSignals

source.where: Table 2-17 UART Pin Descriptions (page 26), Table 2-19 I2C Pin Descriptions (page 28), Table 2-22 PWM Pin Descriptions (page 31), Table 3-1 Power and System Control Pin Descriptions

ports.note: the module's only connector is its 260-pin SO-DIMM edge; every port comes from the generated carrier

source.where: Table 5-1 Recommended Operating Conditions (page 44): VDD_IN (MODULE_ID high) 4.75 min, 20 max

inputV.note: the carrier picks the voltage. MODULE_ID low (a 5 V-only carrier) narrows it to 4.75-5.25 V; 'MAXN_SUPER at 40W for Jetson Orin NX requires minimum 8.0V to the VDD_IN'. Absolute maximum 20.5 V (Table 5-2)

typical.note: no typical current is published; it depends on the power mode and the carrier's VDD_IN

peak.note: the data sheet gives power, not current: divide the mode's budget by the generated carrier's VDD_IN (for example 40 W at 12 V is about 3.3 A, module only)

source.where: front specification table, Operating Requirements: 'Jetson Orin NX 16GB Modes: 10W | 15W | 25W | 40W (MAXN_SUPER)', '8GB Modes: 10W | 15W | 20W | 40W (MAXN_SUPER)'

value.what: 5-20 V from the generated carrier (8 V or more for MAXN_SUPER)

source.where: Table 3-1: VDD_IN 'Main power - Supplies PMIC and other registers', Input, 5V to 20V; 'VDD_IN must be supplied by the carrier board'
Table 2-17 and Table 2-22: UART and PWM/GPIO pins are 'CMOS - 1.8V'; Table 2-19: I2C0/I2C1 'Open Drain - 3.3V'

gpioLevel.note: the module's UART, GPIO and PWM pins are 1.8 V: the generated carrier must level-shift them to the MCU board's 3.3 V

source.where: JetPack 7 Overview: 'JetPack 7 gives you full support for the NVIDIA Jetson Orin and Thor platform' ... 'Built on Linux Kernel 6.8 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS'

os.note: older JetPack 6 images run an older Ubuntu: check the flashed release before picking the ROS 2 distro

also.where: Jetson Linux r39.2.1 (JetPack 7.2) Developer Guide: supported platforms list Orin NX, Orin Nano and the Orin Nano Developer Kit

source.where: Jazzy Jalisco: arm64 / Ubuntu Noble (24.04): Tier 1

ros2.note: Tier 1 is for Ubuntu Noble arm64; JetPack 7 is NVIDIA's build of it, not a stock Ubuntu image

bridgeDevice.via: the MCU board's native USB (CDC-ACM) through a USB port on the generated carrier

source.where: Uploading the Application, note: the USB Serial/JTAG Controller's serial port appears 'as /dev/ttyACM* on Linux'

bridgeDevice.note: the first board to enumerate gets ttyACM0; with several MCU boards, pin each by its USB serial number (a udev rule or /dev/serial/by-id) rather than by order

alternatives.note: NVIDIA's documents name the header UART's signals but not its Linux device; forum answers (not official) point at a /dev/ttyTHS* node, and one reports the TX pin not driving on JetPack 7 (L4T R39.2). Check the node on the flashed image. The data sheet warns: 'The UART receiver input has low baud rate tolerance in 1-stop bit mode. External devices must use two stop bits' (section 2.11.4): set the MCU's UART to 2 stop bits
alternatives.via: UART1 on module pins 203 (TXD) and 205 (RXD), level-shifted by the generated carrier
